figures.name: Bathala

ability.name: Creator's Will
ability.description: Create any one card type from scratch; it enters play with base stats.

figures.description: The supreme creator deity of the Tagalog people, who created the world after a cosmic struggle between sky and sea, ruler of the heavens.

figures.name: Amihan

ability.name: World Wind
ability.description: Rearrange all cards on the field; choose new positions for all allies.

figures.description: The first being in some Tagalog creation myths, a bird who landed between the sky and sea, causing them to separate and create the world.

figures.name: Haliya

ability.name: Silver Moon Shield
ability.description: Create a silver barrier; the first 10 damage dealt to allies this turn is absorbed.

figures.description: The masked goddess of the moonlight who wages eternal war against the moon-eating monster Bakunawa, protecting the moon.

figures.name: Bakunawa

ability.name: Moon Swallow
ability.description: Devour one light-aligned card entirely; the moon darkens, reducing all light powers by 3.

figures.description: The great sea serpent who periodically rises to swallow the moon, causing eclipses; can only be driven back by noise and prayer.

figures.name: Anitun Tabu

ability.name: Capricious Storm
ability.description: Randomly boost or penalize all cards by 1-4 stats; effects are unpredictable.

figures.description: The fickle goddess of wind and rain, daughter of Bathala, whose moods determine the weather, both benevolent and destructive.

figures.name: Amanikable

ability.name: Hunter's Rage
ability.description: Attack all enemies on the field; if you have been denied something this turn, deal double.

figures.description: The ill-tempered god of the sea and patron of hunters, who became hostile toward humans after being rejected in love.

figures.name: Lakan Dula

ability.name: Diplomatic Alliance
ability.description: Form an alliance with one opponent card; it cannot attack you for 3 turns.

figures.description: A great datu and ruler of the Manila kingdom, known for his initial diplomacy with the Spanish before resistance, a hero of his people.

figures.name: Lapu-Lapu

ability.name: Battle of Mactan
ability.description: Deal 10 damage to one foreign invader-type enemy; your people rally with +3 power each.

figures.description: The chieftain of Mactan who defeated and killed Ferdinand Magellan, celebrated as the first Filipino hero who resisted foreign colonization.

figures.name: Maria Makiling

ability.name: Forest Blessing
ability.description: Heal one allied card completely; the forest provides abundant resources for 2 turns.

figures.description: The enchantress of Mount Makiling, guardian of the forests who helps lost travelers and protects nature, but punishes those who exploit it.

figures.name: Bernardo Carpio

ability.name: Mountain Crush
ability.description: Cause an earthquake; all non-stone enemy cards lose 4 defense and are stunned for 1 turn.

figures.description: The sleeping giant hero chained between two mountains, whose movements cause earthquakes; a symbol of Philippine nationalism and inevitable liberation.

figures.name: Tala

ability.name: Star Guidance
ability.description: Guide all allied cards to optimal positions; each gains +2 to their highest stat.

figures.description: The star goddess and daughter of Bathala, associated with the morning star Venus, who lights the night sky for travelers.

figures.name: Hanan

ability.name: First Light
ability.description: Remove all darkness debuffs from allied cards; the dawn refreshes all allies' abilities.

figures.description: The goddess of the morning and daughter of Bathala, whose rising signals hope and new beginnings in Tagalog cosmology.

figures.name: Kapre

ability.name: Ancient Tree
ability.description: Root one enemy card in place for 3 turns; they cannot move or use speed-based abilities.

figures.description: The giant spirit that lives in large trees, smoking a pipe and causing people to get lost; feared but sometimes forming bonds with humans.

figures.name: Tikbalang

ability.name: Wrong Road
ability.description: Cause target enemy card to take a wrong path; they attack an ally instead of you for 1 turn.

figures.description: The half-horse half-human creature that guards the forests and causes travelers to lose their way, eternal trickster of Philippine folklore.

figures.name: Nuno sa Punso

ability.name: Mound Curse
ability.description: Curse one enemy who showed disrespect; they lose 2 to all stats for 3 turns.

figures.description: The small old spirit who lives in termite mounds, who curses those who damage or disrespect his home without asking permission.

figures.name: Aswang

ability.name: Blood Drain
ability.description: Drain life from one enemy card each turn for 3 turns; gain HP equal to drained amount.

figures.description: The most feared creature of Philippine folklore, a shapeshifting monster that preys on the sick and pregnant, taking many terrible forms.

figures.name: Diwata

ability.name: Nature's Gift
ability.description: Grant one allied card a permanent +2 to magic and wisdom.

figures.description: The nature spirits and fairy-like beings of Philippine mythology, beautiful guardians of nature who bless or curse those they encounter.

figures.name: Manananggal

ability.name: Upper Body Flight
ability.description: Separate and fly; deal 8 damage to one enemy while your lower body blocks attacks for you.

figures.description: The terrifying creature that can sever its upper body and fly with bat wings, preying on sleeping pregnant women, one of the most feared Philippine monsters.

figures.name: Hari sa Ilalim ng Dagat

ability.name: Deep Kingdom
ability.description: Drag one enemy card to the ocean floor; they are removed from battle for 2 turns.

figures.description: The king beneath the sea in Tagalog cosmology, ruler of the underwater realm where the dead sometimes reside.

figures.name: Sitan

ability.name: Temptation's Web
ability.description: Offer one enemy card a false bargain; they must choose between losing stats or switching sides.

figures.description: The god of the underworld in Tagalog belief, who tests and tempts souls, assisted by four evil helpers who spread misfortune.
